newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bearish positions executed in FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bearish positions executed in FTSE.

text.p: Activity in UK equity traded options on Tuesday was mainly confined to the FTSE 100 index options as traders took positions ahead of the Federal Reserve's decision on U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
By the close of business around 35,000 FTSE index contracts had been traded out of a total of 45,000 -- which included stock option trades.

The biggest deals in the FTSE were from put option buyers who were either fearing or hoping the stock market will decline further. One such deal was from a buyer of 2,000 June 4075 puts at 4p. Another deal was to buy 1,000 June 4100 puts at 4p.

Also popular were spread trades in FTSE in which options with different terms -- either the strike price, expiry month, or both -- are bought and sold in order to reduce the risk of a straight position.
The biggest deal involved selling 3,500 June 4825 calls at 9p and buying 3,500 June 4925 calls at 1-1/2p in European style FTSE in a bearish vertical spread strategy.
Maximum profit from the deal at expiry will be 7-1/2p -- or the net credit received -- if the FTSE stays below 4825.
At the close of trading on the London stock market, the FTSE index fell 37.7 points to 4607.5.
Over in stock options, one of the larger deals was in mining giant RTZ, where a call spread was traded involving the sale of 500 May 950 calls at 110p and the purchase of 500 May calls at 63p.
The strategy will make a maximum of 47p at expiry if the underlying shares go below 950p. RTZ shares closed down 6p at 1051-1/2p.
Elsewhere in British Telecommunications, the main deals were to close existing positions ahead of Wednesday's May stock options expiry. BT shares fell 5p to 445-1/2p.
-- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7954 *FOR FUTURES AND OPTIONS EXPIRY DATES PLEASE SEE PAGE UKA4 *
